la:adj:sobrius.html:
sōbrĭus (sōbrĕus), a, um (
comp. sobrior, Laber. ap. ; elsewhere not compared), adj.
cf. Gr. σώφρων, σάος; Lat. sanus
, not drunk, sober (freq. and class.).
Lit., opp. vinolentus, ; so ; opp. vino madens,; opp. madidus,; cf. ; Cato Utic. ap. ; and ap. ; opp. ebrius, (with siccus); ; opp. temulentus, et saep.: male sobrius, i. e. ebrius,; .—
Transf., of things (poet. and post-Aug. prose; cf. ebrius): pocula, (24): lympha mixta mero,: nox,in which there was no drinking, (4, 16), 11; cf. convictus,: uva,not intoxicating,: rura,that furnish no wine,; cf. : sobrium vicum Romae dictum putant, vel quod in eo nulla taberna fuerit, vel quod in eo Mercurio lacte, non vino supplicabatur, Fest. pp. 296 and 297 Müll.: non sobria verba,i. e. of a drunken person,: paupertas,: lares pauperes nostros, sed plane sobrios revisamus,.—
In gen., sober, moderate, temperate, continent: parcus ac sobrius,: vigilans ac sollers, sicca, sana, sobria, Afran. ap. (Com. Rel. p. 148 Rib.): homines frugi ac sobrii,: auream quisquis mediocritatem Diligit ... caret invidendā Sobrius aulā,; : non aestimatur voluptas illa Epicuri, quam sobria et sicca sit,: corda,: vetus illa Romana virtus et sobria,; opp. libidinosus,.—
Trop., of the mind, sober, even-minded, clever, sensible, prudent, reasonable, cautious (syn.: mentis compos, sanus): satin' sanus es aut sobrius?; cf.: satis credis sobriam esse,: tu homo non es sobrius,: vigilantes homines, sobrii, industrii,:

diligentes et memores et sobrii oratores, ; opp. iracundus,: alte sobria ferre pedem,prudently,.—Of things: opera Proba et sapiens et sobria,: ingenium siccum ac sobrium,: violenta et rapida Carneades dicebat, modesta Diogenes et sobria,.—Hence, adv.: sōbrĭē (acc. to II. A. and B.).

Moderately, temperately, frugally: vivere (with parce, continenter, severe; opp. diffluere luxuriā),.—
Prudently, sensibly, circumspectly, = prudenter: ut hoc sobrie agatur,: curare aliquid,: hanc rem accurare,; .

sobrius

sobriety (post-Aug.).
Lit., temperance in drinking, ; .— Hence Sobrietas personified,the enemy of Venus,; .—
In gen., moderation, temperance, continence (cf.: modestas, temperantia): vitae,; .—
Trop., reasonableness, prudence: consiliorum,.
